content:
Can your child see the hidden cubes in a stack? Or say which net folds into a dice with opposite faces summing to 7? Visualising Solid Shapes is the IMO’s test of mental rotation. It is wonderfully coachable. Take the free IMO Class 7 Solid Shapes online test below. It has 10 Olympiad-pattern MCQs with instant scoring. Every answer comes with a worked explanation. Aim for 8 out of 10.

What the IMO asks from Solid Shapes in Class 7

  • Faces, edges and vertices of solids.
  • Nets of cubes, cuboids, cylinders and cones.
  • Euler’s relation F + V − E = 2.
  • Views: top, front, side.
  • Cross-sections and shadow shapes.

Key facts and formulas to revise first

  • A cube: 6 faces, 12 edges, 8 vertices — and F + V − E = 6 + 8 − 12 = 2.
  • A cube net always has exactly 6 squares — but not every 6-square arrangement folds.
  • A cylinder’s net: two circles + one rectangle.
  • On a standard dice net, opposite faces sum to 7.

Mistakes that cost Olympiad marks

  • Counting hidden cubes wrongly in stack pictures (work layer by layer).
  • Accepting any 6-square arrangement as a cube net.
  • Confusing edges with vertices in the Euler check.
